parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban or border rejection is documented, and same-sex conduct is not generally criminalised with no Article 331 prosecutions in 2023. Against that, police are documented using the ambiguous Article 331 as a pretext for bribes and false claims of illegality, violence and extortion by state and non-state actors is documented qualitatively, social hostility is high (73% of capital residents dislike a homosexual neighbour), and there is no gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse. Trans-specific tolerance, facilities, custody and care are not documented and are inferred from the hostile general regime. The worst documented feature is state-tolerated police extortion plus hostility with thin recourse, below recurring-harassment cases with working remedies but above cases with an unremedied universal exclusion or organised targeting campaign.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport/visa marker mismatched to presentation has no local route to congruent documentation and no gender-identity discrimination protection. Border acceptance or rejection of foreign markers is not documented.
entry_documents.protection: No law criminalising consensual same-sex conduct; no documented border rejection of trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch, if questioned, interacts with police pretext use of Article 331 and absence of recourse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police invoke Article 331 to solicit bribes from men perceived as gay and falsely claim same-sex activity is generally illegal. Custody or ward placement by birth sex is not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No known arrests or prosecutions under Article 331 in 2023; abuses are investigated when reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Ambiguous under-21 provision gives police leverage during stops that could escalate to detention, but detention practice is undocumented.

care_services.exposure: No documented trans-specific care denial, ward rule, or medication practice; no gender-identity healthcare anti-discrimination law is a resident-facing gap.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 331 scope is ambiguous and treated as basis to justify discrimination; police use it for extortion. Social attitudes are hostile.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same-sex relationships legal since 1940; provision not invoked for prosecutions; where violence is reported law enforcement punishes it.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Dead-letter in prosecution but operative as police pretext and discrimination justification, so statute is a secondary but real lever.

minors_guardians.exposure: Article 331 punishes same-sex acts with a person under 21 (6 months-3 years, fine) versus 18 for different-sex acts; scope ambiguous. Most 2022 violence was by family members, relevant to travelling minors visiting family.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor under 21, or a guardian/minor relationship classed as same-sex, could fall within the ambiguous provision's stated terms.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: NGOs reported psychological and physical harassment and financial extortion by government and non-state actors; violence rose in 2022, committed by state authorities, private citizens and mainly family.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Where violence is reported, law enforcement punishes it; abuses investigated when reported. No hate-crime law, so no bias route.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are both extortion perpetrators and the formal responder to reported violence, limiting effective recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection on sexual orientation or gender identity, no hate-crime law, no legal gender recognition, and sensitive-data law covers sexual orientation/sexual life not gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Investigation of reported police abuses and punishment of reported violence; data protections for sexual orientation in air-passenger and data laws.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of resident machinery is not itself visitor exposure, but absence of bias/discrimination recourse after outing is.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in documented harassment/extortion and absent effective anti-discrimination remedy, but this case lacks a current visitor-setting survey showing large-majority discrimination and lacks a universal facility/custody rule, so it sits above 0.35.

This case is lower than 0.55-C: that anchor has familiar gender-diverse roles and a prosecuted assault, whereas here social hostility is documented, police themselves extort using the ambiguous law, and no bias recourse exists.

Well below 0.75-C: that anchor has a respected gender-diverse role, non-enforcement of the old statute, and court compensation for refusal. Here the statute is used as a police bribe pretext, violence is documented, and no such remedies are documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: generally lawful presence with no prosecutions, but an ambiguous under-21 statute operated by police as extortion leverage, hostile capital attitudes, and documented state/non-state harassment and violence without gender-identity or bias recourse. No universal facility, border, custody or care exposure is documented, so severity is below organised targeting or unremedied tier-1 exclusion. Extrapolating trans-specific risk from the general LGBTQ regime, as trans tolerance is undocumented, places the case in elevated risk, mid-0.4s, with police interaction and family violence the main outing consequences, partly mitigated by investigation/punishment when reported.
